newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Smart sees over 500,000 users by yearend.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Smart sees over 500,000 users by yearend.

text.p: Philippines' Smart Communications Inc is projecting a subscribers' base of more than 500,000 by the end of the year, Smart president Orlando Vea said on Thursday.
"We'll hit more than half a million this year," he told Reuters in an interview. The cellular telephone firm reported that it had 308,000 subscribers by the end of last year.
As of February, the company already reached 362,000 subscribers, overtaking market leader Pilipino Telephone Corp which reported 357,000 subscribers.
Vea said the company has an average 25,000 to 30,000 new subscribers every month due to its aggressive marketing strategy and widening coverage.
"Every month, we are moving in 15 to 20 cellsites," he said. The company had 218 cellsites by the end of last year. It plans to set up at least 200 more this year.
Cellsites are equipment which provide telephone signals for a particular area.
Smart is jointly owned by Metro Pacific Corp, First Pacific Co Ltd and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
It is selling 20 percent of its equity priced at between 12 to 20 pesos through an initial public offering by the middle of the year.
Vea said he expects the company to be listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange by July.
